clue.text: Enjoyment of foreign land

parts.note: de is the French word for of, so a foreign of
to light on something is to land or alight on it

explanation.surface: Someone takes pleasure in a faraway country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foreign' looks like an adjective for 'land', but it goes with 'of': French DE. 'land' is a verb, as a bird lights on a branch.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name great pleasure or joy.

clue.text: Total — two blues

parts.note: feeling blue is feeling down
the second blue is the Tory colour, so politically right

explanation.surface: A sports fan counts up two Oxbridge sportsmen.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue means sad (DOWN) and conservative (RIGHT: blue is the colour of Britain's Conservative Party).
explanation.definitionFit: Total and utter, as in an outright lie or complete fool.

clue.text: Descent of rope taking time

parts.note: a line is a rope or cord
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A climber's slide down a rope takes a long while.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancestry: a line of forebears from whom one is descended.

clue.text: Big support reported for the stars

parts.note: great means big
to bear is to support a weight

explanation.surface: A huge prop is said to be needed for celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' links the wordplay to the definition, a group of stars.
explanation.definitionFit: The constellation Ursa Major, the bright northern star group.

clue.text: Test this Australian can of beer

definitions.meaning: a test ... is the glass vessel used for experiments
Australian slang for a can of beer

explanation.surface: A drinker challenges someone to try a can of Aussie lager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Test this' is read as test + this word, making a laboratory vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A test tube is a narrow glass vessel, and Australians call a can of beer by the same word.

clue.text: Journalist saying "I can be cutting"

parts.note: a hack is a journalist, usually a jobbing one
a saw is an old saying or proverb

explanation.surface: A reporter boasts that his remarks can be sharp.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the tool speaking for itself: a saw for metal says it can cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A toothed hand tool for metal, which cuts as its whole purpose.

clue.text: Hard — dinghy's moved here out of the water

indicators.note: the letters are moved into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the possessive s gives no letter

explanation.surface: A small boat has been hauled up onto dry land.
explanation.walkthrough: HARD DINGHY rearranged gives the answer; 'here' points to the beached boat in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Stranded on land, as a boat left by the tide is beached.

clue.text: While talking, invent a new word for a wedge

indicators.note: the sound of a spoken word is what counts here

parts.note: to coin a word is to invent it

explanation.surface: Someone talking makes up a fresh term for a doorstop.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is an old word for a wedge or a cornerstone.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic word for a wedge or quoin, a cornerstone.

clue.text: Singers giving bribe to a queen

parts.note: a sop is something given to pacify, a bribe
a rani is an Indian queen

explanation.surface: Performers are bribing a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian plural for the highest female voices.

clue.text: Field right in the middle of open country

indicators.note: the single letter is set inside the word for open country

parts.note: a wold is high open rolling country

explanation.surface: A meadow sits right in open countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Field' means a sphere of activity, as in the world of sport. WOLD is an area of open upland, as in the Cotswolds.
explanation.definitionFit: A domain or sphere of activity, as the art world.

clue.text: Shrink half the cotton

indicators.note: only the front five of the ten letters of the fabric's name are kept

parts.note: winceyette is a soft brushed cotton cloth used for nightwear

explanation.surface: Fabric loses half its size in the wash.
explanation.walkthrough: WINCEYETTE is a brushed cotton fabric, popular in Britain for pyjamas and sheets; its first half is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To flinch or recoil is to draw back in pain or distaste.

clue.text: 3 in America taking a ride

definitions.meaning: the American name for the star group of 3 down, the Plough
a roller coaster at a British funfair

explanation.surface: A constellation hitches a lift across the States.
explanation.walkthrough: '3' points to the answer of 3 down, the GREAT BEAR; Americans call its seven bright stars by this name. In Britain the same words mean a roller coaster.
explanation.definitionFit: The Plough is called by this name in the US, and a funfair switchback railway shares it.

clue.text: In truth. I left some property

indicators.note: the word I has been left out, departing from the longer word

parts.note: reality is truth, what actually is

explanation.surface: Someone admits that, honestly, they abandoned part of their estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I left' reads as a confession, but it tells you to drop the letter I from REALITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Real estate, land and buildings, is property in American usage.

clue.text: Gets help? That's denied

parts.note: gains means obtains or gets
aid means help

explanation.surface: Someone who asks for help is refused it.
explanation.definitionFit: To contradict or refuse a claim is to deny it.

clue.text: Very detailed curse placed upon love-child

indicators.note: in a down answer the first word sits above the second

parts.note: blow is a mild curse, as in blow it
a by-blow is an old word for a child born outside marriage

explanation.surface: Someone swears at an illegitimate child.
explanation.definitionFit: Describing every stage in turn, as a commentator does round by round.

clue.text: Bird starts to get rather exhausted by egg-laying

indicators.note: the opening letter of each of the following five words is taken

explanation.surface: A bird becomes worn out from producing eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' applies to all five words from 'get' to 'egg-laying'.
explanation.definitionFit: A diving waterbird with a pointed bill, noted for its courtship displays.

clue.text: This, my lad, can afford great relief

definitions.text: This, my lad, can afford great relief

indicators.note: the letters of the first three words, if rearranged, name a town whose siege was famously lifted

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An elder tells a boy that something will bring him great comfort.
explanation.walkthrough: THIS MY LAD rearranged gives the answer. The Relief of Ladysmith (1900) ended a long Boer War siege of this South African town and was greeted with wild celebration in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The South African town whose siege was lifted in 1900 in a famous British rescue.

clue.text: Stuff fool into tumbledown shack

indicators.note: the word for fool is pushed inside the jumbled letters
a tumbledown shack has fallen apart, so its letters are disordered

parts.note: taken as written
a clot is a fool

explanation.surface: Someone crams an idiot into a ramshackle hut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuff' looks like a verb matching 'Stuff fool into', but it is the noun: cloth. 'tumbledown' is the anagram signal and 'into' the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A coarse fabric, stuff being an old word for woven cloth.

clue.text: It's kept by unmarried American girls under 18

definitions.text: It's kept by unmarried American girls under 18

parts.words: It's kept by unmarried American girls under 18
parts.note: a store for a trousseau kept by a single woman in the US; 18 refers to the TOP DRAWER of 18 across, the British name being the drawer beneath

explanation.surface: Something American teenage girls look after.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under 18' looks like an age but points to 18 across: in Britain the store is the bottom drawer, below the top one.
explanation.definitionFit: The American name for a chest where a woman gathers linen for married life.

clue.text: People of high standing, such as Leonardo da Vinci

definitions.meaning: the upper class, the best people
a supreme artist, a draughtsman of the highest rank

explanation.surface: A Renaissance genius is held up as an example of the elite.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is read literally: Leonardo was a draughtsman of the first rank, a 'top drawer'.
explanation.definitionFit: Upper-class people are said to come from the highest drawer, and a great artist is a first-rate draughtsman.

clue.text: Colourless centre to pattern that's colourful

parts.note: pale means lacking colour

indicators.note: the central three letters of the word pattern are taken

explanation.surface: A drab middle spoils an otherwise bright design.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's board for mixing paints, so the thing holding many hues.

clue.text: Monster seen about, riding horseback

indicators.note: the word for the monster is turned round, facing about

parts.note: an orc is a goblin-like monster of fantasy
a jockey who is riding is said to be up

explanation.surface: A monster has been spotted on horseback nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses the monster to give CRO. 'horseback' is a noun here: the rump of a horse, where a rider might sit behind the saddle.
explanation.definitionFit: The rump or hindquarters of a horse, behind the saddle.

clue.text: In the fresh air to do our exercises

indicators.note: the letters are put through exercises, worked into a new order

explanation.surface: We take our workouts in the open.
explanation.definitionFit: Done outside a building, in the open.

clue.text: Light gold

definitions.meaning: an old lantern with a thick lens on one side
the centre of an archery target, coloured gold

explanation.surface: A pale golden colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A lantern with a convex lens is so named, and the golden centre of a target bears the same name.

clue.text: Fill in short

definitions.meaning: to inform someone, give them the details

explanation.surface: A request to complete a form briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: To brief someone is to inform them, and a brief talk is a short one.

clue.text: Generates passion aboard ship

indicators.note: the word for passion is carried inside the letters for the ship

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
ire is anger, a passion

explanation.surface: Feelings run high on board a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: To father offspring is to beget or produce them.

clue.text: Name about to turn sour

indicators.note: both words are turned backwards, each in place

parts.note: to cite is to name or mention
ca is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: Someone's name is on the point of going off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn' reverses both pieces in place, giving ETIC and AC; the clue lists them in the opposite order to the answer, which takes AC first.
explanation.definitionFit: Like vinegar, which contains the acid of the same root, so sharp-tasting.

clue.text: Dress a Shakespearian servant up

indicators.note: in a down answer, up means the name is read from the bottom

parts.note: Iras is an attendant of Cleopatra in Antony and Cleopatra

explanation.surface: A servant from a play is dressed up in costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns IRAS, Cleopatra's attendant, round.
explanation.definitionFit: A draped garment worn by women in South Asia.

clue.text: Amongst others, king got caught in Italian revolution

indicators.note: the royal letters are trapped inside the jumbled word
a revolution turns everything over, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the regal cipher, read here as king

explanation.surface: A monarch was seized during an uprising in Italy, among other places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' is the anagram signal and 'got caught in' the container signal; ER (Elizabeth Regina) stands for a monarch, though here read as king.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means among other things, used to say a list is not complete.

clue.text: I put on a little weight — it's the bracing air

indicators.note: the letters for the weight are placed in front of the word for I

parts.note: oz is the abbreviation for ounce, a small weight
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker gains a few pounds at the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I put on a little weight' reads as a confession of gaining a few pounds; 'put on' is the charade signal, placing the weight first.
explanation.definitionFit: Seaside air was popularly believed to be rich in this gas and so invigorating.

clue.text: Woodcutter worries about wood at first

parts.note: frets means worries

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word wood is used

explanation.surface: A lumberjack is anxious about the forest.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine-bladed saw for cutting curves in thin wood.

clue.text: Come into it after getting a lot of stick

indicators.note: the word it comes after the shortened word
most of the word is kept, its final letter dropped

parts.note: to inhere is to stick fast within, from the Latin for stick in
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone enters a place after being heavily criticised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of stick' looks like heavy criticism but is INHERE (to stick in) with its last letter dropped. 'Come into' is a phrasal verb: to receive an estate.
explanation.definitionFit: To come into money or property is to receive it as an heir.
